lines.text: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about farm animals!
A cow, a horse and a pig. What can they do?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Put on your farm boots. Let's go!
Who has a tummy with four parts?
Is it the cow? Or is it the lion?
It is the cow!
Here is the fun fact. A cow's stomach has four parts! Four parts, all in one tummy.
Let's count them. One, two, three, four!
What does a cow do with its food after it swallows? Hmm.
It brings the food back up, and chews it again! That is called chewing its cud.
Look at the cow, chewing away.
Grass goes down, comes back up, and gets chewed again. Chew, chew, chew! Down, up, and chew again.
A cow chews its cud for a big part of every day. Lots and lots of chewing!
The biggest part of a cow's stomach can hold twenty-five gallons or more!
That is a lot of room for grass. Wow! A big, big tummy!
Say it with me. A cow's tummy has four parts!
Can you chew like a cow? Chew, chew, chew, nice and slow. Chew, chew.
Now say it like a cow. Moo! Moo! One more time. Moo!
Quick check! How many parts does a cow's stomach have? Four? Or one?
Four! One, two, three, four. Great job!
Who can take a nap, standing up?
Is it the horse? Or is it the monkey?
It is the horse!
Here is the fun fact. A horse can sleep, standing up on its four legs!
Standing still, eyes closed, taking a nap. Shh. Quiet, everyone.
How does a horse stay up while it sleeps? Hmm.
Its legs can lock in place, so it stays steady without falling over!
Look at the horse, standing tall.
But for its deepest sleep, a horse lies down on the ground. Down it goes!
Lying down, all snug. Sweet dreams, horse! Night, night!
Muscles and strong bands in its legs hold the legs steady, with very little work.
So a horse can rest, and still stand tall. Clever horse! Neigh!
Say it with me. A horse can sleep standing up!
Can you stand still like a sleeping horse? Stand tall, and lock your legs. Shh.
Now gallop like a horse. Clip, clop, clip, clop! Clip, clop, clip, clop!
Quick check! Can a horse nap standing up? Yes, or no?
Yes! A horse can nap standing up. You remembered!
Who digs in the dirt with its nose?
Is it the pig? Or is it the lion?
It is the pig!
Here is the fun fact. A pig digs with its snout! Its snout is its nose.
Digging with your nose is called rooting. Root, root, root! Dig, dig, dig!
Why does a pig dig up the dirt? Hmm.
To cool down! A pig loosens the dirt with its snout, and the soft, cool dirt helps it cool off.
Look at that round, pink snout!
Pigs use their noses to say hello, too. When a new pig comes, the other pigs sniff to check it out!
Sniff, sniff! Hello, new friend! Nice to meet you!
A mother pig digs with her snout, to gather things for a cozy nest.
A snout for smelling, for digging, and for saying hello. What a busy nose!
Say it with me. A pig digs with its snout!
Can you wiggle your nose like a pig? Wiggle, wiggle!
Now say it like a pig. Oink, oink! Oink, oink, oink!
Quick check! What does a pig dig with? Its snout? Or its tail?
Its snout! Root, root. Super thinking!
Wow! We met three farm friends. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
Who chews its cud with a four-part tummy?
The cow! Yes!
Who can nap standing up?
The horse! That's right!
Who digs in the dirt with its snout?
The pig! You remembered!
You learned so many new things today.
Chew like a cow. Nap like a horse. And dig like a pig!
Which farm friend is your favorite?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
